card.name: Mennde
card.era: Said to be the last of the seven rhythms to arrive (post-1848 abolition); living tradition
card.tagline: Fast carnival gwoka rhythm of Congo/African origin.
card.profile: Mennde (mende, minde) is one of the seven gwoka base rhythms, a fast, energetic carnival rhythm symbolizing collective celebration and escape (evasion); it incites a marching/parading pace and underlies the polyrhythms of Guadeloupean Carnival. It is said to be the last rhythm to arrive on the island, brought by contracted 'Congos' after the 1848 abolition, and shows strong direct African influence. Played on the ka drums (two boula plus make) with chacha and responsorial Creole song, danced in the lawonn during lewoz gatherings and in carnival processions (Wikipedia: Gwo ka; Mediatheque Caraibe/Lameca).
card.insight: Mennde is the gwoka rhythm most embedded in Carnival; its African/Congo origin story marks it as the most recent addition to the seven-rhythm canon.
